So I'd like to begin by thanking Supervisor Alcorn and the board at large for your interest in scams and your support of issues impacting older and vulnerable adults.

In 2016, growing reports of contractor scams and door-to-door solicitations targeting older adults specifically led to discussions between leaders of the Department of Family Services and the police chief. And out of those discussions came Silver Shield and the Financial Exploitation Task Force.
So I'll be covering the Financial Exploitation Task Force. While Silver Shield has a public-facing prevention focus, the Financial Exploitation Task Force serves an entirely different purpose.

It is a targeted multidisciplinary team that supports a subset of financial exploitation reports received by the Adult Protective Services Program. This also provides a collaborative response to financial exploitation of older and vulnerable adult victims in Fairfax County.

Adult Protective Services, or APS, is a state-mandated social services program housed under the Department of Family Services. APS conducts investigations of reports of abuse, neglect, and financial exploitation of older and vulnerable adults.

The primary goal is to determine if the abuse, neglect, or exploitation has occurred and to offer protective services and programs when the adult is determined to need them and consents to receiving them. APS investigations do not replace the work of law enforcement, nor does APS have the authority to arrest, prosecute perpetrators, or compel adults to cooperate in any investigation or accept services.

However, Virginia Code Subsection 63.2-1605 requires that every financial exploitation report received by APS is also reported to law enforcement. This is accomplished using a centralized email sent to our law enforcement entities, which they then enter into their respective systems, FICOR.

Not every APS financial exploitation, however, is moved forward by law enforcement or assigned to a detective or prosecuted. Admittedly, unknown scammers are quite difficult to prosecute. However, law enforcement partnership continues to provide the guidance expertise needed during task force exploitation meetings, and they are invaluable to the APS investigation process the task force was created out of a desire to support a more comprehensive approach to tackling financial exploitation specifically and the framework was based on a Philadelphia

financial exploitation task force model this multidisciplinary case review model focuses on the role that partnership plays in supporting older adults both in the short term and in the long term Fairfax added on to the framework by adding a spotlight presentation, which helped draw awareness and training to the various agencies and entities and their relevant contributions, services, and supports to provide a more informed perspective. The National Association of Adult Protective Services and the Administration for Community Living, which was the federal agency at the time that oversaw Adult

Protective Services, provided support to the Task Force Steering Committee, and technical assistance was received from the Department of Justice's Elder Justice Initiative in creating and building out the task force. It was determined by leadership at the time that APS would serve as the lead for the task force and the Board of Supervisors actually supported the creation of a new position at the time to focus squarely on financial exploitation cases and matters. The APS Financial Exploitation Coordinator, Raina Hill, who is actually here with us today, now facilitates The task force works in partnership with Silver Shield to support this endeavor.

The task force members meet monthly and review cases brought forward by APS staff. They tend to be the most egregious of the financial exploitation cases that are received, and they receive guidance from the various members. Key members, of course, include our land development services partners, as well as law enforcement civilian investigators, the Office of the County Attorney, the Department of Family Services Domestic and Sexual Violence Services Program, The Department of Cable and Community Affairs, the Virginia Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation, the U.S. Postal Service, as well as the FBI.

There are other members, but these are the key ones. In fiscal year 24, approximately $19 million in losses were reported by the 159 APS financial exploitation victims alone.

With the support of the task force, about 20% of those losses were able to be recovered for those victims, but clearly we have more work to do. Some are used to help victims secure their accounts, provide financial counseling, reconcile accounts, and set up automated payments to further secure their resources. Other resources are focused on providing counseling service, and that is really to address the emotional impact of victimization. There's a lot of stigma associated with this crime. So our domestic and sexual violence support services through our Department of Family Services helps provide that specifically to our romance scam victims.

The role of artificial intelligence and cryptocurrency has added new elements that make this even more difficult to investigate and makes perpetrators that much more elusive. The Financial Exploitation Task Force continues to stay abreast of strategies to strengthen investigations and to encourage and advocate for stronger prosecution and recovery efforts wherever possible.

APS will continue its partnership with Silver Shield campaign, focusing on prevention and drawing the community's awareness to scams and how individuals can protect themselves against all types of exploitation.
